text: 这波半导体回调大约持续到中期大选，大佬是怎么看的

$LITE
 CEO interview on demand, counterparty + financing risk:  

- "CFO of 
$GOOGL
 came on and reported capex going up Y/Y, we expect hyperscalers for report an increase in capex in earnings. 

Based on what we see, we see their spend going up."

- "The purchase agreements we have, to a large degree, are noncancellable."

- The difference between Lumentum and companies like 
$AVGO
, "we are not as dependent on AI datacenter buildout going forward"

There's a conversion between electrical products to optical products" creating structural demand. 

Q: When do you see able to see yourself having more inventory? (catching up to surge in demand)

- When we look at demand, there is "no end in sight" 

TLDR:

Financing risk and demand aren't equally distributed across AI supply chains. But markets are just selling everything off together. 

As for photonics in specific, I said this before, but  increasing optical content per XPU + CPO/NPO adoption keeps going up so we'll likely see sector spend go up, even if aggregate capex goes down.

There's the usual "no end to demand in sight" commentary, but 
$LITE
 does have capacity commitments into 2029 now... and are negotiating for 2030. (with new information that most of which are likely hyperscalers + non-cancellable) 

So doesn't quite sound like it's all over for the AI trade, especially photonics.

Last time I've seen "It's all over" type posts was... 3 months ago during the situational awareness liquidation. 

And... 3 months ago before that... with Iran tensions + Oil + Helium + LNG fears/pricing. 

And... few months ago before that. I'm sure everyone remembers Deepseek

Last major $SIVE disclosure was 100M CW DFB laser capacity Q4 2027. And a new foundry partner (that makes 2 including Win Semi).

Expected 
$JBL
 revenue coming in H1 2027 (with lasers for Jabil's 1.6T LRO scaling up H2 2027).

There's channel checks along the way like CIOE where Sivers was engaged with Chinese pluggable makers + laser ASPs being raised.

70mW/100mW ranges were the most tight to Chinese pluggable makers, which was surprising.

Biggest industry read through was 
$LITE
 selling out into 2029, making agreements for 2030, and having hyperscalers pay for capacity expansion for 2031. 

I don't think anyone has enough information to do any sort of accurate modeling for $SIVE like you can for 
$AAOI
 given they don't release product breakdown + capacity targets by quarter.

The 200mW NPO lasers Sivers is sampling is likely different ASP than your 70mW lasers shipped to pluggable makers. And your custom CPO lasers are different pricing too. 

Like all sampling/qualification players from 
$AEHR
 to 
$AAOI
 back in 2025, usually the risk/reward comes in whether qualifications convert and what new customers they have, which is always a risk. 

In a bull case, if $SIVE comes online with 300m laser supply (2:1 implied ratio, already has "tremendous" supply online from likely US fab) during a structural shortage.  

Pluggable players like 
$JBL
, 6 other vendors.  


$GFS
 as the reference design laser for their CPO/NPO platform. 

Your minor players vendors like 
$POET
, 
$AEVA
 and other players end up scaling.

And all the other custom products they hinted they were working on in the past for CPO years back.  

I think the probability that they cook is higher since there's so many ongoing qualifications during a bottleneck. 

We've already seen ownership changes from Swedish investors to US/International retail from $SIVE shareholder disclosures. 

My guess is that trends institutional from retail before US listing next year amid the market correction. 

Think people forgot institutions have already financed their expansion, which was a 700M SEK round 100%+ ago (multiple times oversubscribed). 

And that $SIVE uses primarily external fabs, so it's not the same as a lot of the major financing concerns affecting Neoclouds. 

Anyway, up to management execution, I'm not running Sivers so no clue what other companies are working with them now, whether it's Cambridge or some other US player like Semtec.

TLDR:

- Just need to wait for earnings for more disclosures around qualifications + partners, only so much public can guess from channel checks and supplier mapping.
